Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =2x$, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡2x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5-8{cos}^{2}⁡2x)\text{d}x & =\int [5-8\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1)]\text{d}x \\  & =\int [5-4(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1)]\text{d}x \\  & =\int (1-4\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)\text{d}x \\  & =x-4(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x)+C \\  & =x-\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
